subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for legacy ownerless session rows, matching the existing delete ownership fence, even though upgrades may stop plugins that previously patched those rows?
rationale: No safe automatic migration can infer which plugin owns an existing ownerless row, so preserving compatibility versus enforcing the isolation boundary requires explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Enforce fail-closed ownership
options.body: Approve ownerless-row rejection for plugin-runtime callers, keep operator and non-plugin recovery available, and document the upgrade boundary in the PR context.

options.title: Preserve ownerless compatibility
options.body: Allow plugin-runtime patches on ownerless rows temporarily, accepting weaker isolation until a maintainer-defined migration or deprecation path exists.

options.title: Pause for migration design
options.body: Hold the PR until an operator or doctor workflow can safely assign or retire legacy ownerless rows.

recommendation.title: Enforce fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Approve ownerless-row rejection for plugin-runtime callers, keep operator and non-plugin recovery available, and document the upgrade boundary in the PR context.

likelyOwner.reason: Tak Hoffman has the strongest adjacent merged history around session ownership metadata and preservation semantics.
